notes: The temp test tests/unit/features/zzAudit.security.test.js was created, run and deleted. Job-id authorisation is sound: getJob filters by owner, ids carry 144 random bits, and history is scoped to the user. The cache only holds public data (robots files, archive lookups), so no account sees another's data through it. Left out: the in-memory cache and wayback maps never evict, shared learning_stats can be skewed by other accounts, and connector failure messages logged at deepCheck.js:698 may carry query text (not verified).

findings.title: Page reader fetches private, loopback and metadata addresses; redirects are followed before any check
findings.evidence: Temp test: readable() returned true for 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1:3009, localhost:3009, [::1], 192.168.1.1. plan({kind:'domain',value:'127.0.0.1'}) and 'metadata.google.internal' each produced a lookup. http.js uses redirect:'follow', and readable(landed) only runs after the fetch.
findings.scenario: Anyone can edit a Wikidata 'official website', or a page with the person's name can carry a JSON-LD sameAs of http://127.0.0.1:3009/api/founder?name=x+y. Either becomes a trusted url or domain thread, so the server sends GETs to internal hosts. A public URL that 302s to an internal address is fetched before the check runs.
findings.fix: Add a safeTarget(url) check in http.js: http or https only, ports 80/443 only, refuse IP literals in private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT or ULA ranges, refuse .internal/.local/localhost, and refuse hosts whose DNS lookup resolves into those ranges. Set redirect:'manual' and check every hop again (at most 5). Add tests.
findings.verifyNote: readable() only checks scheme, NEVER list, broker hosts; no private/loopback/link-local filter. http.js uses redirect:'follow', and openPage checks readable(landed) only after the internal hop was fetched. robots.txt on the internal host is requested first too. Blind SSRF, e.g. to localhost:3009 locally.
findings.betterFix: Validate in http.js for every request (robots, archive, pages): http(s), ports 80/443, no IP literals or names in private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, ULA or IPv4-mapped ranges, no localhost/.internal/.local. Check the resolved address at connect time with an undici Agent connect.lookup hook so DNS rebinding is closed. Use redirect:'manual', re-check each hop (max 5) and add tests.

findings.title: htmlToText is quadratic on unclosed <script> or <!--, so one hostile page can freeze the server
findings.evidence: Temp test: htmlToText('<!--'.repeat(n)): 80 KB took 1.2 s and 160 KB took 4.7 s. '<script>' x40k (320 KB) took 1.5 s. The page reader accepts up to 3 MB, and pageText runs before the name check.
findings.scenario: A page the reader opens (from a search headline, Wikidata or sameAs) serves 3 MB of '<!--' or '<script>' with nothing closing them. The lazy [\s\S]*? backtracking blocks the event loop for minutes. Timeouts cannot fire, the step dies at maxDuration, and other requests on that instance stall.
findings.fix: Replace the regex block stripping with a single linear scan using indexOf for each opener and its closer. Once an opener has no closer, drop the rest of the text. Cap the input given to htmlToText and structuredData at about 1 MB. Add a timing test with 1 MB of '<!--' that must finish in under 200 ms.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced in scratch: the same two regexes took 1.9 s on 160 KB of '<!--' and 7.6 s on 320 KB. The growth is quadratic, so 3 MB (the reader's maxBytes) would block the event loop for minutes. pageText/stripBlocks run on any opened page.
findings.betterFix: As proposed (a linear indexOf scan, and drop the tail when there is no closer). Also audit stripBlocks, structuredData and the line-360 <title> regex for the same lazy [\s\S]*? pattern, cap html at about 1 MB before any parsing, and add a 1 MB timing test.

findings.title: The quick brief (/api/founder) needs no sign-in and has no rate limit, and each call spends metered search and model allowances
findings.evidence: The handler never checks a session before runFounderCheck. founderCheck.js:702-715 runs 6 web queries per name variant through searchWeb (Serper/Tavily), plus CourtListener and an LLM brief. The repo has no rate limiter for this route.
findings.scenario: A script or a cross-site calls the GET in a loop. Each call makes 6-12 metered searches and a model call lasting up to 60 s. The shared allowances drain, the deep check's last-resort search and the briefs fail for the owner, and the person's name goes into access logs through the query string.
findings.fix: Require sign-in, or apply a per-IP-label limit when signed out, using the founder_jobs pattern or a small founder_quick_hits table (for example 20 an hour per account and a global hourly cap). Move the call to POST with a JSON body so names stay out of URLs and logs, and set Cache-Control no-store on every response.
findings.verifyNote: index.js calls runFounderCheck with no session or rate check. It is a GET with the name in the query string, so a cross-site or a loop triggers metered searches and model calls. No limiter exists in the repo.
findings.betterFix: Keep it usable signed out if the owner wants that, but add a per-IP-label hourly limit (clientLabel plus a small table) and a global hourly cap. Sign-in or the allow-list should lift the per-IP limit. Move it to POST with a JSON body (this also stops cross-site triggers) and set no-store on every response, errors included.

findings.title: Any Google account can sign in and run deep checks on anyone, with no allow-list and no global cap
findings.evidence: The signIn callback always returns true. deep.js limits only per account (12 an hour). Any stranger with a Google account counts as 'signed in', and the debug routes treat sign-in as authorisation too.
findings.scenario: A stranger signs in with throwaway Google accounts and runs 12 checks an hour on each, on private individuals. The tool then works as a public people-profiler on the owner's site, and the free and metered allowances go to strangers.
findings.fix: Add FOUNDER_ALLOWED_EMAILS (and/or an allowed domain) checked in signIn and in a requireFounderUser() helper used by founder/deep, founder/history and the debug routes. Add a global cap of checks per hour across all accounts, counted in founder_jobs. Tell refused users that the check is not enabled for their account.
findings.verifyNote: The signIn callback always returns true. deep.js limits per account only (12/hr), and the debug routes accept any session. The owner says the site is non-commercial; an allow-list is cheap and fits the privacy rules.
findings.betterFix: As proposed. Make the allow-list an environment variable, fail closed in production when it is unset, keep ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN local only, and add a global hourly cap counted in founder_jobs.

findings.title: Parallel 'step' or 'brief' calls on one job each repeat the full 40 s of outbound work; in memory mode they mutate one shared state
findings.evidence: step loads the job and runs stepDeepCheck. Only the save checks rev, so losers get a 409 after all their requests have gone out. In memory mode getJob returns the stored object (same state reference), and saveJob ignores expectRev.
findings.scenario: A client retry, a second tab or a script sends 20 concurrent steps for one jobId. That makes 20x the lookups against every source and bypasses the 12-checks-an-hour limit's purpose. Locally (the owner's test setup) two overlapping steps run on the same state object, which corrupts the queue, tasksRun and the findings.
findings.fix: Take a lease before working. Run UPDATE founder_jobs SET lease_until=now()+interval '55 s' WHERE id=$1 AND user_id=$2 AND (lease_until IS NULL OR lease_until<now()) RETURNING state, and answer 409 when it returns no row. In memory mode keep a per-id lease map and deep-clone state in getJob. Release the lease on save. Treat 'brief' the same way.
findings.verifyNote: In memory mode, getJob returns the stored record whose state is the shared object, and saveJob ignores expectRev, so overlapping steps mutate the same state. In DB mode the rev check runs only at save, after all outbound requests were sent. Proposed lease is feasible.

findings.title: A response without Content-Length is read in full before the size check
findings.evidence: Temp test with a chunked 21 MB stream and maxBytes 2 MB: all 21 chunks were pulled, and only then 'Response larger than 2 MB' was thrown. response.text() is called before text.length is compared with the limit.
findings.scenario: A hostile or broken page the reader opens streams gigabytes with no Content-Length for 12 s. The function buffers all of it, runs out of memory and kills the step, and parallel lookups on the instance die with it.
findings.fix: Read response.body with getReader(), count the bytes, and cancel the reader and abort the controller once the count passes the limit, then throw tooLarge(). Decode with TextDecoder in streaming mode. Keep the current error message so honest-coverage notes stay the same.
findings.verifyNote: http.js calls response.text() and compares text.length afterwards; with no Content-Length the whole body is buffered first. text.length also counts UTF-16 units, not bytes. Streaming reader with cancel is the right fix.

findings.title: Per-host pacing and back-off live in process memory only, so concurrent checks on other instances break Crawl-delay
findings.evidence: nextSlot, restUntil and lastRest are module Maps. On Vercel each concurrent request may run on its own instance. LittleSis and the Gazette publish Crawl-delay 10 and the archive allows about 15 a minute, but two checks (or parallel steps) on two instances each pace on their own.
findings.scenario: Three users run checks at once on three instances. LittleSis receives three requests inside 10 s and web.archive.org about 45 a minute. Those hosts then refuse or ban the client, and later checks report failed sources. This breaks the polite-access rule.
findings.fix: For hosts with a gap of 1 s or more, reserve slots in the database: a host_slots table updated with UPDATE ... SET next_at=greatest(next_at,now())+gap RETURNING the wait. Share 'rest' state there too. Keep the in-memory path for the default 120 ms hosts.
findings.verifyNote: nextSlot/restUntil/lastRest are module Maps, so pacing is per instance. But steps of one check are sequential, usage is a few accounts, and Vercel often reuses instances, so a Crawl-delay breach needs concurrent checks across instances. The gap is real; medium overstates it.
findings.betterFix: A DB slot table only for hosts with a gap of 1 s or more, as proposed. Cheaper alternative: cap concurrent running checks globally (also covered by the global cap in open-signup) so cross-instance overlap on slow hosts is rare.

findings.title: Debug routes run model calls with no sign-in on previews and no limit for any signed-in account, and reveal the configuration
findings.evidence: open = NODE_ENV!=='production' || VERCEL_ENV==='preview' skips sign-in, relying on Vercel's preview protection being on, which is unverified. In production any Google account may call ?run=brief|gaps (up to 50 s of model calls) with no limit. env-check lists which provider variables are present or missing.
findings.scenario: Someone loops GET /api/debug/llm-check?run=gaps on the preview URL, or signed in on production, and uses up the free model allowances. Briefs then fall back to quoted text. env-check shows strangers which search and model services are set up.
findings.fix: Allow the debug routes only for the owner allow-list (FOUNDER_ALLOWED_EMAILS) in every environment except NODE_ENV=development. Add a per-account limit (for example 10 runs an hour), and return 404 rather than 401 to everyone else.
findings.verifyNote: llm-check is open whenever VERCEL_ENV==='preview' (relying on unverified preview protection), and in production any session can run brief/gaps model calls with no limit. env-check reveals which providers are configured to any signed-in user.
findings.betterFix: As proposed: owner allow-list outside NODE_ENV=development, a 404 for everyone else, and a small per-account run limit. Do not rely on Vercel preview protection.

findings.title: The name and company inputs accept control, bidi and zero-width characters, search operators, emails and one-letter tokens
findings.evidence: normalizePersonName only strips quotes and collapses whitespace. The only checks are 2 or more tokens and 120 characters or fewer. 'a b', 'x site:example.com', 'jo@x.com y' and names containing U+202E or U+200B all pass. The company is not cleaned beyond whitespace.
findings.scenario: 'J S' starts a 420-lookup check that matches every page. 'Jane Roe -fraud' or 'Jane site:x.com' rewrites all ~15 query patterns. An email or phone turns the check into a people-search. A bidi override makes the History list show a different name.
findings.fix: Use one validator for both routes. Apply NFKC, strip Cc/Cf characters (control, zero-width, bidi), and allow only letters, marks, space, hyphen, apostrophe and period. Require at least two tokens, the last at least 2 letters. Reject '@', digits, ':' and URLs in names. For the company, strip Cc/Cf and search operators (site:, a leading -, OR). Return a clear message for each rejection.
findings.verifyNote: normalizePersonName only strips quotes and possessive 's and collapses whitespace. The routes check only for 2 or more tokens and a 120-character limit, so control, bidi and zero-width characters, operators, emails and one-letter tokens all pass. The company only has whitespace collapsed.
findings.betterFix: As proposed, using Unicode classes (\p{L}\p{M}) so non-Latin names pass. Do not require the last token to be 2 or more letters; that rejects real names such as 'Malcolm X'. Instead require at least one token of 2 or more letters and reject names made only of initials. Quote the company in queries as well as cleaning it.

findings.title: The 72-hour retention is not enforced on read: old reports stay readable until someone starts a new check
findings.evidence: The DELETE of old founder_jobs rows runs only inside createJob. getJob and listFinishedChecks never check updated_at, so a report about a person outlives the stated retention whenever no new check is started.
findings.scenario: An account runs a check and no one starts another for a week. GET /api/founder/deep?jobId= and /api/founder/history still return the full report seven days later, contrary to 'kept 72 hours'.
findings.fix: Add AND updated_at > now() - interval '72 hours' to the getJob and listFinishedChecks queries, and run the same age filter in memory mode. Optionally add a Vercel cron that deletes expired rows daily.
findings.verifyNote: The DELETE runs only in createJob (DB), and forgetOldInMemory runs only in createJob (memory). getJob and listFinishedChecks never filter on age, so a report outlives the stated 72 hours whenever no new check starts.

findings.title: FOUNDER_DEEP_PUBLIC is not blocked in production, and the anonymous owner is taken from the first x-forwarded-for value
findings.evidence: ownerOf honours FOUNDER_DEEP_PUBLIC whatever NODE_ENV is. clientIp takes the left-most x-forwarded-for entry, which the client sets on any host that only appends to the header.
findings.scenario: If the flag is ever set on Vercel or another host, anyone can run deep checks. Outside Vercel, a new X-Forwarded-For value per request gives a fresh 12-an-hour allowance each time.
findings.fix: Honour the flag only when NODE_ENV==='development'. Take the client address from x-real-ip or x-vercel-forwarded-for, or from the right-most trusted hop, with the socket address as the fallback.
findings.verifyNote: ownerOf honours FOUNDER_DEEP_PUBLIC in any environment, and clientIp takes the left-most x-forwarded-for value, which the client controls behind proxies that append to the header. The handover only says 'never set in Vercel'; there is no code guard.

findings.title: No security response headers on the site
findings.evidence: next.config.js defines no headers() and the repo has no middleware. Pages that show third-party quotes and links send no X-Content-Type-Options, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy.
findings.scenario: Another site can frame /founder (clickjacking a signed-in user into starting checks). Without Referrer-Policy, in-page navigation can leak query strings to linked sites.
findings.fix: Add headers(): X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors 'none' (start in report-only for a full CSP), Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and Permissions-Policy camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=().
findings.verifyNote: next.config.js has no headers() and there is no middleware file, so no frame-ancestors, nosniff, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy headers are sent.

findings.title: makeFinding accepts any URL scheme, and React 18 still renders javascript: hrefs
findings.evidence: Line 116 only requires that url is truthy. DeepCheck.js:127/139/310 render f.url and profile links straight into href. React 18 only warns about javascript: URLs. Today's sources happen to filter schemes; there is no central guarantee.
findings.scenario: A future connector maps a field the publisher controls (a feed item, an API 'url' field) into a finding with javascript:… or data:…. Clicking the record runs script on the site's origin, with the user's session and network view.
findings.fix: In makeFinding and makeThread, drop any finding or thread whose url is not http(s), and normalise it with new URL(). Add a registry test that fails when a connector emits another scheme.
findings.verifyNote: makeFinding checks only that url is truthy, and sanitizeFinding checks blocked hosts only. DeepCheck renders f.url, m.url and profile links into href, and React 18 only warns on javascript: URLs. Today this is defence in depth only.
findings.betterFix: As proposed, plus a render-side guard (a safeHref helper in DeepCheck.js and founder.js) so saved reports created before the change are covered too.
